description_full: Avio S.p.A. designs, develops, produces, and integrates space launchers in Italy and internationally. The company involved in the design, development, and production of solid and liquid propulsion systems for launchers; design, development, and production of solid propulsion systems for tactical missiles; development, integration, and supply of complete light space launchers; research and development of new environmentally friendly propulsion systems and attitude control engines for satellites; liquid propulsion systems for satellites; and ground infrastructure for launcher preparation and launch. Avio S.p.A. was founded in 1984 and is headquartered in Colleferro, Italy.

financial_summary: AVIO SPA is a small-cap industrials business with a $1.7B market cap on $644M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +19% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 2% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 71% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $137M in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 16.04× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 27× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 24.8% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 28% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
